land.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

successors.note: 'The war ended in January 1894 with a victory of Leopold's Force Publique.' The page does not say the Free State annexed Maniema or Tanganyika, only that Kasongo was 'Tippu Tip's capital in Maniema' and that Rumaliza dominated Tanganyika from Ujiji.

capitals.name: Kasongo
capitals.note: Coordinates from the gazetteer's Kasongo. Congo Arab war page: 'Tippu Tip's capital in Maniema, the city was 35 miles south of Nyangwe'; Tippu Tip page: he 'came to rule a large territory in the eastern Congo, centered on the town of Kasongo'. Kasongo fell to Dhanis on 22 April 1893.

correction.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no such domain): 'Between 1884 and 1887, he claimed the Eastern Congo for himself and for the Sultan of Zanzibar' and 'came to rule a large territory in the eastern Congo, centered on the town of Kasongo'. No area is given by any page; Maniema province (111,000 km2) is a proxy for the Kasongo-Nyangwe core. The Tanganyika coast (Rumaliza's Ujiji) and the Stanley Falls district lie outside it (confidence 1).

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1884: Tippu Tip claims the eastern Congo. 'Between 1884 and 1887, he claimed the Eastern Congo for himself and for the Sultan of Zanzibar.' The trade posts began earlier (his first expedition set out in 1867 and in 1868 he was in Ugalla), but no page dates the domain's founding; 1884 is the claim.

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1887 February 24: Tippu Tip becomes governor of the Stanley Falls District for the Congo Free State. 'In early 1887, Stanley arrived in Zanzibar and proposed that Tippu Tip be made governor of the Stanley Falls District'; 'on February 24, 1887, Tippu Tip accepted.' The domain stays Arab-Swahili in practice; the vassal tint is the suzerain's to record (congo-free-state with counterpart this slug). [Reviewer af-06, 2026-10-19: type changed from rename to vassal_start with counterpart congo-free-state, the mirror of congo-free-state's vassal_start of February 1887]

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1892 March: Sefu bin Hamid begins attacking the Free State, ending the client relation. 'In March and April 1892, Tippu Tip's son Sefu bin Hamid began attacking Congo Free State personnel in eastern Congo' (Congo Arab war page); Tippu Tip had retired to Zanzibar in 1891 (Tippu Tip page). [Reviewer af-06, 2026-10-19: added as the mirror of congo-free-state's vassal_end of March 1892]

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1892 November: open war between Sefu bin Hamid and the Free State. 'Open warfare broke out in late November 1892, when Sefu set up a fort on the Lomami River'; Sefu had attacked Free State personnel in March and April 1892, and by October he led about 10,000 men.

region.text: Nyangwe, 35 miles north of Kasongo, on the Lualaba

ledger.note: 1893 March 4: Nyangwe falls. 'On 4 March, the Free State forces crossed the river using 100 dugout canoes'; the defenders fled and the city fell 'largely without resistance'.
1893 April 22: Kasongo falls. 'Dhanis advanced up the river to Kasongo on 22 April 1893', and the city fell within two hours; Sefu was killed in the battle on the Luama River on 20 October 1893.

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1894 January: the war ends. 'The war ended in January 1894 with a victory of Leopold's Force Publique': Belgian reinforcements under Captain Lothaire arrived on 9 January and 'within three days, the remaining forts ... surrendered'.

region.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

ledger.note: 1894 January: the last Arab-Swahili forts surrender and the domain ends. The tens of thousands of dead included combatants and civilians; 'the market around Nyangwe ceased to exist, while the city of Kasongo was all but destroyed'. Rumaliza fled to German territory in 1895 (Tippu Tip page).

wars.name: Stanley Falls clash of 1886
wars.outcome: 'In 1886 ... fighting broke out between the Swahili and the representatives of King Leopold II of Belgium at Stanley Falls'; Tippu Tip, in Zanzibar, then reassured the Belgian consul.
wars.note: The page gives no territorial result.

wars.name: Congo Arab war

zones.text: Maniema, the eastern Congo around Kasongo and Nyangwe

wars.outcome: Free State victory: Nyangwe fell on 4 March 1893, Kasongo on 22 April 1893, Sefu was killed on 20 October 1893 and the last forts surrendered in January 1894 (remnants executed in December 1894).

certainty.note: A trading domain of posts and caravan routes with no frontier.

notes: Cliopatria has no Arab-Swahili domain in the Congo. No page gives an area or a boundary; Maniema province is the proxy for the Kasongo-Nyangwe core. The page lists Tippu Tip's start as a claim of 1884, but his posts are older (1867, 1868). The Tippu Tip page gives 1891 for his return to Zanzibar. Rumaliza's Tanganyika domain at Ujiji (in German East Africa), Kabambare (Maniema; the advance is undated) and the Stanley Falls district are not drawn. The Sultan of Zanzibar's claim over the domain (1884-1887) belongs to the Zanzibar dossier (vassal_start counterpart this slug). Page budget (2-5): two pages.
